chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Back at the Three Deuces; the March of Time film; Tiny's Exercise
summary: At the Three Deuces everyone came to hear them; they appeared in a March of Time short, and he explains how Tiny's Exercise came from a practice riff.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You left Los Angeles with Tatum for New York with Tatum and played at 52nd street.

Yeah we went to a place called the Three Deuces. I think I mentioned that. Stayed there weeks and weeks. Everyone used to come down there. A great singer used to come down there every night. Bailey, Mildred Bailey used to come down there all the time. I mean everybody came there, no way around that. We even did The March of Dimes or March of Times or somethin there. . . . They show it every now and then now. . . . We were in and out, we left there like I said, we went out west, come back, some place.
March of Time, was that a film short?
My song, Tiny's Exercise, sure did.
When did you write that tune, was it while you were with Tatum?
I believe so, I think so, yeah. I'm quite sure of it.
Did it start as an exercise?
Well when I would be practicing this riff came out. And I just named it that.

Because it sounds somethin' like an exercise, not that I could read an exercise. That's the way it came out. I just added a few more touches & changed the music. It came out pretty good. Tatum liked it. He played it all the time. Only thing, it was my tune but he played it too fast, ha ha, I could hardly keep up with it. Ike Quebec -- I made it with him also.
